classification.difficultyReason: Factor both vectors and explain their common direction using scalar multiples.

content.prompt:
$\overrightarrow{AB}=4\underset{\sim}{a}+6\underset{\sim}{b}$ and $\overrightarrow{CD}=10\underset{\sim}{a}+15\underset{\sim}{b}$.

Show that $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{CD}$ are parallel.

answer.short: $\overrightarrow{AB}=2(2\underset{\sim}{a}+3\underset{\sim}{b})$ and $\overrightarrow{CD}=5(2\underset{\sim}{a}+3\underset{\sim}{b})$, so the vectors are parallel.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{AB}&=4\underset{\sim}{a}+6\underset{\sim}{b}\\&=2(2\underset{\sim}{a}+3\underset{\sim}{b})\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{CD}&=10\underset{\sim}{a}+15\underset{\sim}{b}\\&=5(2\underset{\sim}{a}+3\underset{\sim}{b})\end{aligned}$$
Both vectors are scalar multiples of $2\underset{\sim}{a}+3\underset{\sim}{b}$, so they are parallel.
